solution: When you have a mix of decimals, fractions, and mixed numbers, the easiest way to order them is to convert every value to a decimal first so they are all in the same form. $\\[1em]$ Tip: to turn a fraction into a decimal, divide the numerator by the denominator. For example, $\frac{7}{8} = 7 \div 8 = 0.875$. For a mixed number, do the same with the fractional part and add it to the whole. $\\[1em]$ Apply this to each value: $\\[1em]$ $4/7$: divide $4 \div 7 = 0.571429$ $\\[1em]$ $6/9$: divide $6 \div 9 = 0.666667$ $\\[1em]$ $0.82$ is already a decimal: $0.82$ $\\[1em]$ $1/4$: divide $1 \div 4 = 0.25$

Now line the decimal forms up vertically so the decimal points stack on top of each other. For example, $\frac{7}{8} = 7 \div 8 = 0.875$. For a mixed number, do the same with the fractional part and add it to the whole. $\\[1em]$ Apply this to each value: $\\[1em]$ $4/8$: divide $4 \div 8 = 0.5$ $\\[1em]$ $1/2$: divide $1 \div 2 = 0.5$ $\\[1em]$ $0.1$ is already a decimal: $0.1$ $\\[1em]$ $0.66$ is already a decimal: $0.66$

Now line the decimal forms up vertically so the decimal points stack on top of each other. Fill any short tail with placeholder zeros so every number has the same number of decimal places — that way you can read down the columns digit by digit. $\\[1em]$ $0.50$ $\\[1em]$ $0.50$ $\\[1em]$ $0.10$ $\\[1em]$ $0.66$

Compare the whole-number parts first, then the tenths, then the hundredths, etc., to put the decimal forms in order. $\\[1em]$ $0.1 < 0.5 < 0.5 < 0.66$. $\\[1em]$ Translating back to the original numbers: $0.1 < 4/8 < 1/2 < 0.66$.
